issues.title: Lab analysis visits follow CRF labels, not the SAP actual-date visit windows
issues.summary: SAP page 11 assigns laboratory assessments to visits by actual date, with nearest-target and tie rules; the specification maps collected visit labels and no lab window table exists.
issues.expected: SAP p.11: lab assessments are assigned to visits by actual visit date; the one closest to the target day is selected, and the earlier one when two are equidistant.
issues.observed: The specification maps LB.VISIT labels and has no window, nearest-target or tie rule. The SAP window table gives no lab windows, so the rule cannot be run. The Pilot 6 R reimplementation also maps labels.
issues.action: Decide whether lab visits use CRF labels or date windows; for windows, document lab target days and windows and implement them, otherwise amend the SAP.

citations.quote: The ADAS-Cog (11), CIBIC+, and NPI-X assessments will also be assigned to visits based on the actual visit dates, as will laboratory assessments.

If multiple assessments fall into the same visit window (windows 
defined in following table), then the assessment closest to the target day will be selected.

If two assessments are equidistant from the 
target day, then the assessment prior to the target day will be selected.

In general, assessments will be assigned to visits as collected on the CRFs, and will 
disregard the actual date of the assessment.
Hematology, and clinical chemistry will be summarized for Baseline and Weeks 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, and 26 (Visits 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 13, respectively).

mutate( AVISIT = case_when( ABLFL == "Y" ~ "Baseline", grepl("UNSCHEDULED", VISIT) == TRUE ~ "", TRUE ~ str_to_sentence(VISIT) ), AVISITN = case_when( AVISIT == "Baseline" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", AVISIT)) ), AENTMTFL = "" ) %>% rbind(eot) %>% mutate( AVISITN = ifelse(AVISITN == -1, "", AVISITN) )

# get EOT for those that did not make it to week 24 eot2 <- adlb06 %>% arrange(STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAMCD, desc(AVISITN)) %>% group_by(STUDYID, USUBJID, PARAMCD) %>% filter(VISITNUM != 13) %>% slice(1) %>% filter(!is.na(AVISITN), AVISITN != 0, AVISITN != 99) %>% mutate( AVISITN = 99, AVISIT = "End of Treatment", AENTMTFL = "Y" )

issues.title: Threshold distance formula: Define omits absolute values, the specification reverses signs
issues.summary: Define-XML takes the larger of the signed terms LBSTRESN-1.5*ULN and .5*LLN-LBSTRESN; the Pilot 6 R reimplementation adlbc.r takes absolute values; the specification negates both terms.
issues.expected: Define-XML ADLBC.ALBTRVAL: Maximum of [LBSTRESN-(1.5*ULN)] and [(.5*LLN) - LBSTRESN], significant digits 3.
issues.observed: The Define rule differs from the reference on 74244 of 74264 records; the larger absolute distance, as adlbc.r L193-L195 computes, reproduces all 74264. The specification uses 1.5*A1HI-AVAL and AVAL-0.5*A1LO.
issues.action: Decide whether the threshold distance is signed or absolute, correct the Define-XML formula to it, and align both specification row branches.
